chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys meat from the market, and among his brothers there is one who slaughters and sells it, yet he deliberately buys from the 'Nassab' (those who set enmity). He said: 'What thing do you ask me to say? He eats nothing but like the dead body (jaththah), blood, and meat of the pig.' I said: 'Glory be to Allah, like the dead body, blood, and meat of the pig?' He said: 'Yes, and greater than that is with Allah.' Then he said: 'Indeed, this is in his heart against the believers, a sickness.'

key_terms.الدَّمِ: Blood, another primary category of impure food.
key_terms.النَّصَابِ: The 'Nassab' (those who set enmity), a specific group or type of seller known for their enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt or believers.
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: Carrion or dead animal not slaughtered ritually, a primary category of impure food.
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: Meat of the pig, a primary category of impure food.
key_terms.مَرَضٌ: Sickness, used metaphorically here to describe the spiritual defect of enmity in the heart.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on meat from the 'Nassab' and why is it significant?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the status of the 'Nassab'—specifically those who harbored enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt and the believers—by equating their meat to the major impurities of carrion, blood, and pork. He emphasizes that while the physical ruling is similar, the spiritual gravity is greater because their enmity constitutes a 'disease' (marad) in the heart, reflecting the Shia concept of *tawalla* and *tabarra* where theological allegiance impacts ritual purity. This ruling underscores the link between spiritual state and physical consumption in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
